_comment.1: Open-loop plant Bode of the x/tilt axis: command -> FSM -> camera -> CoM.
_comment.2: PARPORT-DAC version of conf_bode_x.json -- identical camera/CoM/sweep, with
_comment.3: anyloop:piplate_bridge swapped for anyloop:parport_dac (DAC81404 over the
_comment.4: PCIe parallel card). Everything downstream of the command is unchanged, so
_comment.5: this measures the SAME plant through a FASTER transport.
_comment.6: WHY THIS SWEEP EXISTS: the delay in steering_fsp.json / attenuation_fsp.json
_comment.7: was measured with the BRIDGEplate in the loop. The parport DAC replaces a
_comment.8: ~0.5-1.4 ms serial write with a ~12.8 us two-channel bit-bang, so the plant's
_comment.9: tau is expected to DROP by a meaningful number of frames. Run this (and the
_comment.10: y twin) BEFORE trusting steering_par_fsp.json's delay -- that file carries
_comment.11: the piplate-era value on purpose, see its _delay_warning.
_comment.12: K MUST BE RE-MEASURED -- it does NOT carry over from the piplate era.
_comment.13: Two independent reasons: (a) the fine channel is DIVIDED downstream, so a
_comment.14: given DAC volt no longer reaches the FSM as the same volt it used to, and
_comment.15: (b) scale here is 1.0 V/unit against the piplate config's 2.0, which halves
_comment.16: the volts per command unit on its own. The <=30 Hz |H| plateau this sweep
_comment.17: produces IS the new Kx. Expect it well below the old 0.915.
_comment.18: SOFTWARE injection: bode_plot replaces the x element (1; CoM is [y, x])
_comment.19: with a sine each iteration, and parport_dac writes offset + sine*scale to
_comment.20: DAC channel 1 (DACB) every cycle. Range 0-5 V, offset 2.5 V and scale
_comment.21: -1.0 V/unit, so amplitude 0.1 sweeps 2.4..2.6 V: 2.5 V +/- 100 mV.
_comment.22: No PID in the loop, so the command IS the sine = open loop. Phase is
_comment.23: from wall-clock time and includes the full transport delay.
_comment.24: TWO channels only -- there is no coarse stage. ch0 = y/tip, ch1 = x/tilt.
_comment.25: y is parked at the 2.5 V bias (scale 0) while x is swept.
_comment.26: CHECK sample_rate against the achieved loop rate before believing tau: the
_comment.27: value below is inherited from the piplate era. The camera should still be
_comment.28: the bottleneck, but the DAC no longer adds to the period.

params._roi_note: ROI centred on beam at coarse bias 2/2 (fine 1.5/2.15): probe-verified 2026-07-21, full-sensor CoM (x 919, y 507). Re-derive via contrib/probe_frame.json only on an alignment change.

pipeline._comment: frame -> UDP viewer, so you can watch the beam + tracking (same as steering_fsp)

params._note: tracked 20x20 window, threshold 22 -- matches conf_bode_x.json exactly so the parport sweep measures the same sensor the piplate sweep did. Initialized on the beam (frame centre) with no acquisition phase: bode_plot injects from the first frame, and the stray reflection at ROI (10,28) must stay out of the sum. Output is image-normalized.

pipeline._comment: CoM -> UDP viewer so the tracked centroid can be overlaid on the frame
Replace the x/tilt element (1) with the swept sine; read CoM x as response

params._tuning: v2 (2026-07-17): 60 log points x 49 cycles, split into 7 integer-cycle segments per point. The segment scatter gives the per-point error bar + a coherence quality (1=clean; <0.9 flagged as a disturbance line or drift inside the window). Integer-cycle segment boundaries (on excitation-phase crossings) kill the partial-cycle DC/line leakage the old fixed-time cutoff left in. 49 cycles keeps the 5 Hz window ~10 s, resolving it from the 5.64 Hz line.
params._amplitude: scale is 1.0 V/unit and offset 0 V, so amplitude IS the drive in volts: 0.1 = +/-100 mV about the 0 V mid-range bias, i.e. the output sweeps -0.1 to .1 V. Keep scale at 1.0 in every config that shares this K -- amplitude only reads as volts because command units ARE volts.
params._amplitude2: half-amplitude (+/-50 mV, i.e. -.05 to .05 V) linearity/dead-zone check: if |H| moves between the two, the CoM has left its linear region or the FSM is in its dead-zone, and K is not trustworthy. bode_plot flags >10%. The converter is NOT a candidate cause -- the excursion is ~2600 codes at 76 uV/LSB, sitting at mid-range with 2.4 V of headroom either side.
params._avoid_freqs: nudge sweep points off the measured bench lines (a line inside the lock-in skirt biases the point coherently -- segments do not average it out). List from attenuation6/8 memory.
params.config: x/tilt open-loop plant through the PARPORT DAC (DAC81404, spi link, mmio, range 0-5 V on a +/-12 V supply), no coarse stage, ch0=y / ch1=x. Drive 2.5 V +/- 100 mV, i.e. 2.4..2.6 V (scale -1.0 V/unit, offset 2.5, amplitude 0.1). 32x32 exp250 gain100 bw100, beam-centred ROI via start_x/start_y, tracked 20x20 thr22. Purpose: derive BOTH Kx and tau for this transport from scratch. tau: expect SHORTER than the piplate-era 5.8 fr, since the ~0.5-1.4 ms serial write is now a ~6.4 us bit-bang. Kx: expect WELL BELOW the old 0.915 -- the fine channel is divided downstream and scale is halved (1.0 vs 2.0 V/unit), so the old value is not a prediction, only an upper bound. K uses <=30 Hz; tau uses the full 5-300 Hz phase slope, so the sweep must run to 300.
params._start_delay: hold injection at 0 (= the channel parked at 0 V) for 30 s before the sweep starts. There is no coarse stage to settle any more, but the hold is kept: it gives the FSM and the camera AGC a quiet, known starting point, and bode_plot measures its baseline during it.
params._output_file: distinct filename on purpose: do NOT overwrite the piplate-era fsm_bodex_722_full7.pdf -- the whole point is comparing the two transports.

pipeline._note: PARPORT DAC. TWO channels only -- there is no coarse stage: ch0 = y/tip (DACA), ch1 = x/tilt (DACB). Here y is parked (scale 0) and x is driven.
pipeline._range: 0-5 (unipolar, DACRANGE code 0x0), biased at mid-range 2.5 V so the command has 2.5 V of headroom in BOTH directions without needing a bipolar range. 76 uV/LSB over the 5 V span -- 2x finer than +-5 would give, since the whole 16 bits now cover 5 V instead of 10. The 2.4..2.6 V sweep is ~2600 codes, plenty of resolution and nowhere near either rail.
pipeline._avss_note: AVSS MUST BE -12 V (NOT grounded) on this rig: the steering configs auto-range to +-10 so the mirror can be driven negative on an impact, and the supply is shared. That means this 0-5 sweep also runs with a negative AVSS, which is OUTSIDE the condition SLASEH2A 7.5 characterizes the unipolar figures at (TUE +-0.07 %FSR, offset, zero-code 0.15 %FSR are given at AVSS = 0 V; the -21.5 V <= AVSS < 0 rows are the bipolar ones). It is inside Recommended Operating Conditions (7.3: AVDD 4.5..41.5, AVSS -21.5..0, AVDD-AVSS 4.5..43) and the bipolar TUE at negative AVSS is tighter, so the part is likely fine -- but the bode measures the plant THROUGH this converter, so if absolute gain accuracy ever looks suspect, this is one thing that is not datasheet-guaranteed.
pipeline._footroom_note: The 1.25-1.5 V output headroom/footroom figure does NOT set a floor here: SLASEH2A 7.5 conditions it on -10 mA <= load <= 10 mA (1.25 V) or +-15 mA (1.5 V). Unloaded -- the EC table's own condition, and near enough true when driving an amplifier input -- zero code sits within the 0.15 %FSR zero-code error, about 7.5 mV of ground on a 5 V range. Only if the FSM driver actually pulls ~10 mA AND the output must reach 0 V under that load does a negative AVSS buy anything, and then it costs the characterized condition above.
pipeline._scale_sign: x keeps the NEGATIVE sign the piplate config used (was -2, now -1.0). That inversion is a property of the optical/mechanical path, not of the converter, so it carries over even though the magnitude does not. It is what made Kx come out sign-positive. If the push test now says otherwise, fix it HERE and re-run -- do not fix it by flipping the sign of K.

params._no_range_max: auto-ranging deliberately NOT enabled for a sweep. A mid-sweep range change would glitch the output for a frame and step the quantization, both of which land straight in the lock-in as a bogus data point. The sweep never leaves 2.4..2.6 V anyway, deep inside 0-5. Note the STEERING configs DO auto-range (range_max +-10) -- the bode measures the plant at a fixed 0-5 range and fixed 76 uV/LSB on purpose, so K and tau are not entangled with a range change.
params._verify: off in a swept/timed run: verify turns each write into 3 frames (write, read-command, NOP) plus a non-posted status read per bit. Use it in a bench smoke config, not here.
params._skip_unchanged: still worth having, but expect it to skip far LESS than on the BRIDGEplate: at 153 uV/LSB a swept sine changes the code almost every iteration, where 1 mV codes often repeated. Costs ~6.4 us/frame, against a ~264 us loop period.
params._sync_update: left off. Only ONE channel is driven in this sweep, so there is no inter-channel skew to remove and sync_update would just add a SOFT-LDAC frame per iteration.
